messages:
maria-customer: Hey team — our app started returning intermittent 403 + big latency spikes around 09:12 UTC. Dashboard shows traffic hitting eu-west endpoints even though our VPC is in us-west-2 and our onprem VPN is supposed to egress to US hub. Billing also spiked because tokens billed at EU rates. Anyone seen this pattern?

anna-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and a traceroute from your bastion? Also your tenant id and a sample request id if you have one.

maria-customer: repro below. request id: req_0a3f9c. Tenant: acme-retail-prod. curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` Traceroute (from bastion): ```traceroute to api.redwood.ai (13.35.121.9), 30 hops max. 1 10.0.0.1 0.6 ms 0.5 ms 0.4 ms 2 198.51.100.14 5.2 ms 4.9 ms 5.1 ms 3 203.0.113.2 60.1 ms 58.9 ms 59.5 ms 4 92.60.34.1 62.3 ms 61.9 ms 62.5 ms 5 52.18.200.12 63.0 ms 62.8 ms 62.7 ms (eu-west peer)```

lee-netops: That hop 52.18.200.12 looks like one of our peering circuits that terminates in EU. Do you have SNAT on your onprem gateway? If your SNAT IP pool maps to a tenant tag that prefers the partner transit, egress could be routed to EU. Can you share the NAT translation table or iptables-save?

maria-customer: we do SNAT on the ASA box. here's the NAT rule snippet (sanitized): ```object network SNAT_POOL range 198.51.100.0 198.51.100.255 nat (inside,outside) dynamic 198.51.100.200-198.51.100.220 route-map PREF_EU permit 10 match ip address TENANT_ACME set tag 200``` Not sure why route-map PREF_EU exists — we asked for US-only.

sam-eng: Quick note: our token validation service is region-aware and falls back to the first compatible control plane it can reach. If the request lands at EU ingestion, token is validated against EU tenant mapping which in some edge cases returns 403 because the tenant metadata expected us-west-enabled. That would explain 403s + billing in EU.

anna-support: To repro on our side: can you run a curl with "--resolve api.redwood.ai:443:13.35.121.9" from your bastion and post tcpdump of the 10 seconds after the request? Also include X-Forwarded-For header you see.

maria-customer: ran that, tcpdump attached (pasted trimmed). shows packets going to 52.18.200.12 and we see SNATed src 198.51.100.205. Headers from server side show: ```X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-ID: req_0a3f9c
X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.205```

lee-netops: Aha — route-map PREF_EU is explicitly tagging traffic with set tag 200. Our peering controller has a policy: if incoming SNAT tag == 200, prefer eu-west annoucement. Looks like this NAT configuration accidentally tags the pool for EU peering.

sam-eng: Short term workaround: you can set the header x-redwood-region: us-west-2 on your requests; that bypasses regional selection if authenticated and pins to the requested control plane for token validation. It's not ideal long term because it requires client changes.

anna-support: Adding repro steps we used: 1) curl with --resolve to the VIP from bastion, 2) tcpdump on bastion, 3) compare X-Redwood-Region in the response. We saw 100% repro when SNAT pool had tag 200.

maria-customer: thanks — we removed the route-map PREF_EU and swapped SNAT pool to 198.51.101.0/24 (untagged). Re-testing now...

ops-bot: deploy.event: egress-route-policy-change by maria-customer at 2026-03-17T10:45:02Z

lee-netops: Nice. After untagging can you share a traceroute again? We want to confirm next hop goes to our US hub.

maria-customer: traceroute now: ```traceroute to api.redwood.ai (13.35.121.9), 30 hops max. 1 10.0.0.1 0.7 ms 0.6 ms 0.6 ms 2 198.51.101.14 4.8 ms 4.6 ms 4.7 ms 3 198.51.101.1 5.2 ms 5.0 ms 5.1 ms 4 52.22.110.5 6.0 ms 5.9 ms 6.1 ms (us-west hub)```

sam-eng: Confirmed on our side: requests for req_0a3f9c afterwards show X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2 and 200 OK. No further EU billing. 

anna-support: Glad that's resolved. Action items: - maria-customer: keep the untagged SNAT pool in prod and monitor for 24h - lee-netops: we should add a check in our peering controller to surface unexpected SNAT tag -> region mappings in the onboarding UI - sam-eng: note token validation fallthrough case in runbook so support can advise x-redwood-region header as temp mitigation

maria-customer: will monitor, thanks all :thumbsup:

lee-netops: Filed follow-up ticket NETOPS-642 to add UI validation and a daily audit of SNAT tags.

sam-eng: adding runbook note now.

anna-support: closing the thread once you confirm 24h stable, otherwise re-open.

maria-customer: update after 6h: stable, no EU hits, latency back to baseline. closing for now. thank you! :heart:
